note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, authored none of the change). RFC 5549 Section 4: "A BGP speaker MUST only advertise to a BGP peer the IPv4 or VPN-IPv4 NLRI with an IPv6 Next Hop if the BGP speaker has first ascertained via BGP Capability Advertisement that the BGP peer supports the Extended Next Hop Encoding capability for the relevant AFI/SAFI pair." 238bdb62e9 (spec-refuse-instead-of-defaulting) changed nlri.NewINET to take an explicit has-path-id flag; the unit passes false where it passed path id 0, which already meant no ADD-PATH identifier, so the input, the route and every assertion are byte-for-byte the same (TestRFC8950ExplicitIPv6NextHopFollowsTheNegotiatedPair, both tags). The capability-gated IPv6 next-hop assertions are unchanged; 1dbfd1d7b7 only added OPEN-order tests beside TestNegotiateExtendedNextHop, whose units are byte-identical. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. Independent Section 4 rejudgment retains enforced for this superseded RFC8950-4-1 obligation. TestNegotiateExtendedNextHop and TestNegotiateExtendedNextHopMismatch establish advertised tuple intersection and remote absence. The tagged canUseNextHopFor, self and explicit-next-hop tests distinguish the exact 1/1 and 1/128 tuples, including wrong-pair and absent refusal. TestRFC8950ExplicitIPv6NextHopFollowsTheNegotiatedPair installs the same real negotiated result in Session, Peer and send context and checks API refusal with no unlicensed unicast UPDATE. VPN assertions in that test remain resolver assertions, not VPN socket assertions. Negotiate projects the exact tuple to EncodingCaps; resolveNextHop/canUseNextHopFor and both forwarding consumers use that pair. The successor’s separately tagged forwarding and post-policy final-writer tests provide the shared integration evidence. No stale producer-halt record is treated as selective semantic proof.
